what_happened: ALL SEVEN $0 gates passed, including the read-only transport gate: the bundle round-tripped to the session commit carrying this authorization and executable set. The launcher then failed inside create() because --image defaulted to POD_IMAGE, which is the deployment-commands MAPPING and not an image reference, putting a dict on the provider command line.
what_it_exposed: The more serious finding is that it reached create() AT ALL under --dry-run. Nothing in the shared SessionRunner consulted the flag: run() went from the prechecks straight to create(), so every launcher in this repository advertising 'run every $0 gate and stop before provider creation' would have created a billing pod once its gates passed. The flag was safe only when a gate refused first. Now implemented in shared core with its own test file, including a guards-the-guard case asserting that WITHOUT the flag create() is still reached.
